tasks.short: Agree session times and places with families, plan the route between sessions, travel to homes, libraries or schools, get set up on arrival and claim travel costs.

steps.what: Tutor agrees session times and places with families by phone and messages
Tutor plans the route between the day's sessions
Tutor travels to students' homes, libraries or schools to conduct tutoring sessions
Tutor signs in at the school or library and sets up the room
Tutor fills in the monthly travel claim with kilometres per trip

tasks.design: Families book from the tutor's open slots in the booking tool ({OTHER}), each slot tied to a place, so fewer calls go back and forth. The tutor's open slots are grouped by area to keep routes short. The booking tool lists each trip with its distance, which fills the monthly travel claim in the expense tool ({EXPENSE}) for the tutor to check. Travelling and setting up stay with the tutor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Times and places were agreed by phone, and kilometres were added up by hand each month.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking tools offer self-service slots with places, and expense tools take trip lists.
tasks.still_hard: Families cancel late; the tutor still rearranges by phone.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing to tutor at the library because home is too noisy for this student.

reach.learn: Whether booking by area cuts travel time.

evidence.claim: Momoyoga combines a class schedule, online booking and payment, memberships and attendance reports.
Home addresses of minors' families are personal data; keep them to what booking needs.

assumptions: Boundary: from agreeing times to the travel claim; the session itself is outside.
Input contract: availability entered by families in the booking tool; slot areas set by the tutor; fallback is phone and spreadsheet.
Travelling and setting up do not change.
Families' time is outside the tutor's savings.
unknowns: Sessions away from home per week.
research_questions: Does travel time per session fall?

already_counted.description: Tutor checks the trip list before claiming.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is travel.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare a diagnostic test, administer and proctor it, score closed and open items, write a result summary and send it to the parents.

steps.what: Tutor prepares the diagnostic test for the student's subject and level
Tutor administers and proctors the academic or diagnostic assessments
Tutor scores closed items against the answer key
Tutor scores open answers and judges the student's level
Tutor writes the result summary for the parents
Tutor e-mails the result summary to the parents

tasks.design: The tutor picks a diagnostic test from the published set on the practice platform ({LMS}); students answer there, closed items are scored against the key and a summary template fills scores per topic. The tutor scores open answers, judges the level and writes the conclusion; once the tutor has checked the summary, it goes to the parents. No AI scores or judges.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tests were printed, scored by hand and summaries written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice platforms hold diagnostic tests and score closed items.
tasks.still_hard: A nervous student scores below their level; the tutor must weigh that.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing from the working that the student understands but rushes.

reach.learn: Whether topic scores make referrals clearer.

evidence.claim: Practice platforms hold diagnostic tests and score closed items against a key.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes in education institutions is high-risk; fixed answer keys are not AI.

assumptions: Boundary: from preparing the test to the result shared; the tutoring plan is outside.
Input contract: diagnostic tests from the platform's published set; fallback is printed tests.
Proctoring and judging do not change.
Parents' time is outside the tutor's savings.
research_questions: Are summaries sent sooner after the test?

already_counted.description: Tutor checks the chosen test fits the student.

incremental.description: Tutor sets up test sessions on the platform.

approvals.approved_version: The result summary as checked by the tutor in s5; changes need a new check before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Proctoring and open answers stay manual.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search for suitable textbooks, apps and equipment, try them out, choose what fits, write the recommendation and send it to the parents.

steps.what: Tutor researches textbooks, software and learning materials on publishers' sites and forums

loop.input: The subject, level and exam of the student, and the agency's catalogue of reviewed books, apps and official exam pages.
loop.output: A short list of catalogue items with the catalogue line each choice rests on.
loop.check: Code accepts only items in the catalogue and links to their catalogue entry; the tutor reads every suggestion.
loop.stop: One list per question; no match means the tutor searches by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions are free text about a student's needs; a filter alone misses fit.

steps.what: Tutor tries out new books and apps before recommending them
Tutor chooses which materials to recommend for this student
Tutor writes the recommendation with prices and where to buy
Tutor e-mails the recommendation to the parents

tasks.design: An answer desk over the agency's catalogue of reviewed books, apps and official exam pages ({DOCS}) suggests a short list for the student's subject, level and exam, each linked to its catalogue entry; the tutor reads every suggestion. A template fills the chosen items with price and where to buy, and once the tutor has checked it, it goes to the parents. Trying materials and choosing stay with the tutor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each search started from scratch on publishers' sites and forums.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models can answer questions over a curated catalogue and cite its entries.
tasks.still_hard: The catalogue goes stale unless someone keeps it current.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which app a student will actually open at home.
tasks.altitude: The tutor reads a short list instead of searching from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether tutors' tryouts improve the catalogue.

evidence.claim: Answer desks over a curated catalogue and official exam pages can suggest textbooks and exam guidance.
An AI tool that talks to students or parents must say it is AI from 2 August 2026; this desk serves the tutor only.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student's needs to the recommendation sent; buying is outside.
Input contract: catalogue kept by the tutoring coordinator; student needs from the tutoring plan; fallback is searching by hand.
Trying and choosing do not change.
No student data go into the answer desk beyond subject, level and exam.
research_questions: How often does the tutor pick from the short list?

incremental.description: Tutoring coordinator keeps the catalogue current.
Tutor adds reviews of tried materials to the catalogue.

approvals.approved_version: The recommendation as checked by the tutor in s4; changes need a new check before sending.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Trying and choosing materials stay with the tutor.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The tutor keeps travel, proctoring, judging levels and choosing materials; calls, hand scoring and open searches shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A tutor whose admin fits in the gaps between sessions.
